You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md,.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/dispatch-runbook.md` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #35784: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #35790: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `283450f576029360085b29983cf8991d6713cf79`
  · the check-runs on `283450f576029360085b29983cf8991d6713cf79`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md,.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/dispatch-runbook.md;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

Rule change — a `hits` path sits under `.claude/**`: the PR body declares `Rule-change:` and you verify it against the diff.
  Write `Rule-change-verified: none` ONLY when no changed hunk alters what an agent may do without the maintainer
  (merge, bypass a check, change repository settings), what gets done and in what order (grading, dispatch, scope), or
  what must go to him (decisions, maintainer actions); process steps, scripts, wording, slimming and file moves are not rule
  changes. Write `ruled` ONLY when every such hunk copies the ruling the PR body quotes on its `Ruling-ref:` line — check the
  copy against the quoted words, do not re-rule it. Otherwise `yes`: the pull request then waits for the maintainer.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `SCRATCHPAD/pr-35790/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with `claude/issue-35784-thread-routing-by-size` and `Reviewed-by:` with `session_01L6bhgTRf6qBRCqPh4JZaZL` — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.

Focus for ④, added by the area: the ruling is comment 7033659866 on the card. Does every changed hunk COPY that ruling and nothing more (S as sub-agent in the seat or an area; M into a fitting area, else a thread; big cards one thread each as the runbook already defines them; disclosure-discipline security cards stay in the seat; p1 and `security` set order only)? Do the big-card and disclosure-discipline lines read as before? Were the three same-file deletions that paid the bytes genuine restatement with a surviving home (`os-dev.md`, `AGENTS.md`), or did a rule lose its only home? Does any other line under `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/**` still tie p1 or `security` to `mode:thread` (the area-lease hand-out line is carded separately as #35792 and is out of this diff)?

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (L1-a)

## 维护者速读

- 这次改的是派发技能里「什么卡单开线程」的两句话：以后只看卡的大小和形态，p1 和安全卡只决定先做哪张，不再因为标了 p1 就单开一个线程。
- 对你和用户：产品无变化；车队内部小卡少付一次「重新克隆、重读整份开发说明」的起步成本。大卡、改契约的卡、需要保密的安全卡照旧单开或留在席位。
- 风险：只是规则文字；最坏是某张中卡本该单开线程却进了区，可随时整段撤回。为腾出字节删掉的三处重复说明，我逐条核过，原事实在别处都还在。
- 要你做什么：这是受管规则文本，L2 记录落下后批准一次即可（现读 Tier H，L2 写 `Rule-change-verified: ruled` 后转 Tier S）。

**Head reviewed:** `283450f576029360085b29983cf8991d6713cf79` (1 commit, +6/−6, 2 files under `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/`). Merges cleanly onto origin/main `f44758b2` (`git merge-tree` clean); main has not touched either file or either ratchet script since the PR's base `c99156ee`.

### Ruling fit (7033659866, 「只看大小,p1 只管先后」)

- `dispatch-runbook.md:120`: M cards go to a fitting area, else one thread; `p1`/`security` set order only and never open a thread on their own. This matches the ruling, and the card's Done-when that neither file routes to thread by p1/security alone.
- `security` in "only sets order" is backed by the question the maintainer answered (「p1，安全卡只是优先级，不代表复杂度」). The disclosure-discipline line (`dispatch-runbook.md:124`) still keeps secret-bearing security cards in the seat, so the ruled exception survives unchanged.
- `SKILL.md:69` `mode:` row: big cards and M cards with no fitting area → `thread`; it defers to the runbook section. This agrees with line 120 and with `execution-duties.md` (`S 级机械 + M ⇒ mode:subagent`).
- The big-card line (121–122) is byte-identical; its `同上` now reads against `一卡一线程` on line 120, which is still stated. The S line now adds `或进区`, consistent with the ruling's "S → sub-agent in seat or area".

### Cut list — every deleted fact still has a home (checked at this head)

| Cut | Home found |
|---|---|
| `裁决引文照抄不译;` (SKILL.md) | `SKILL.md:106` keeps 裁决引文 as one of the three Chinese channels; AGENTS.md Communication keeps quote-verbatim |
| `分支约定仍是 claude/issue-N-SLUG;` (runbook) | `AGENTS.md:398`, `AGENTS.md:466`; `.claude/agents/os-dev.md:27` (worktree recipe), `:370` |
| `:请审是席位交棒` (runbook:129) | `SKILL.md:203` 「③ 请审 = 席位交棒」; runbook:129 still forbids threads from assigning or requesting review |

### Gates measured here

- `node scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs`: all ticks; no ceiling or pin row touched; `declared cross-file moves: 0, total ceilings unchanged`. The byte drop is paid inside the same files (as the PR body says: SKILL.md 33863/33872, runbook 20067/20070, widest row 341/pin 341).
- `node scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`: 60 authored bundle files within ceilings.
- `node --use-env-proxy scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35790`: `.claude/**` ×2 → **Tier H now**, because no contract-review record names this head yet. Size 12 lines, under the human-merge threshold.
- CI at this head: 48 check runs, all `success` or `skipped`. None failing or pending, including `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` and `Check Changeset` (skip-changeset).
- PR body: `Fixes #35784`, `Rule-change: ruled`, `Ruling-ref: 7033659866`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. The 维护者速读 is present and in business terms.

### Findings

None blocking. Nit (no action needed): the ruling's consequence text names only p1 for "order"; `security` rides on the maintainer's question. The disclosure line keeps the one security route that was ruled to stay.

### Landing terms

1. The isolated L2 (brief 7046571094) owes a same-head record that reads `Rule-change-verified: ruled`. After that, `check-governed-merges` should read Tier S. Re-run it before landing.
2. L1 does not replace L2. A new push needs a delta L1; a clean main merge keeps this ACCEPT.
3. This review does not approve, mark ready, enqueue or request review; those steps belong to the seat.

Rule-change-verified: ruled

### ① Derived judgments

- Inputs read: card #35784 (body and all four comments: ruling record 7033659866, claim 7033717566, triage 7033762371, dev report 7034046369); PR #35790 body, file list and net diff against `main`; the check-runs on the head.
- Net diff: two files, +6 −6, both under `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/`. `main` has not moved either file, `AGENTS.md`, `os-dev.md` or the ratchet script since the merge base, so the three-dot diff is the net diff.
- Face: rules (governed `.claude/**`). This tier and a declared rule change are both right.
- Accept-set and public surface: no change. The diff holds no schema, no code and no published skill (`skills/**` is untouched). `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body and the claim are right.
- Check-runs on the head: 48 runs, 23 success and 25 skipped (23 names), none red, none pending. `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` and `Lint · repo & tooling gates` are among the green ones. Their conclusions answer the derived gate families.
- Byte ratchet, read off the tree: `SKILL.md` 33872 → 33863 against ceiling 33872; `dispatch-runbook.md` 20070 → 20067 against ceiling 20070; the `mode:` row is 272 bytes against the 341 pin. `check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` is not in the diff, so no ceiling or pin row moved.

### ② Semver level

- Nothing publishes: both files are internal agent tooling under `.claude/`. `skip-changeset` is on the PR and `Check Changeset` is green. No changeset is the right level.
- The `Clause-②: no` line is right: the diff widens no accept-set and enlarges no public surface.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report 7034046369: `open_questions` is empty and `security_findings` is `none`. Nothing to answer there.
- Its two out-of-scope notes: (a) no other p1 or `security` tie to `mode:thread`, confirmed by my own sweep in ④; (b) `Fixes` on body line 2 and the requester on line 3 is PR-body order, and `PR-body guards` is green. No action on either.
- The PR body flags that the big-card line's 同上 now leans on the new first line. Answered as N1 in ④.
- SQL push-down: no code in the diff, nothing to check.
- Raised by this review; no dev flag covers it. The ruling's sentence gives M cards one route, 「M 卡有区进区」, and reserves 一卡一线程 with 「大卡才」. It does not say where an M card goes when no area fits it. The diff keeps `main`'s thread for that case, and the card body and the seat's reading under the ruling record say the same. Kept behaviour needs no ruling, so this does not move the rule-change line. If the maintainer meant that an M card never gets its own thread, that is one more routing change and owes its own card and his word. For the seat to carry; not decided here.
- Seat-side, not the diff: the claim built a `SKILL.md` line at the default tier. `execution-duties.md` allows that downgrade for a line-level text change on the governed surface, with a review at the contract-review tier as its compensating control; this record is that control. The claim's `Container & model:` line also spells a model identifier where the claim template asks for the tier word.
- Seat-side, PR body: the 速读's last line asks for one approval, while the body's own Acceptance notes put the PR at Tier S on a `ruled` record, which `SKILL.md` 路径分叉 does not hand to a person. The seat's final 速读 should carry one of the two.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**The ruling, as recorded in 7033659866 (verbatim).** Choice: 「只看大小,p1 只管先后」. Its stated consequence: 「S 卡用子代理,M 卡有区进区,大卡才一卡一线程;有披露纪律的安全卡仍留座位。要立卡改技能这一行。」 The question before it: 「p1，安全卡只是优先级，不代表复杂度，为什么一定要不进区？」 The PR body's `Ruling-ref:` line quotes the choice and the question exactly as the record has them.

**`references/dispatch-runbook.md`**

- Line 120, routing. Old: on a project-thread seat, M and above, p1 and `security` each get a thread. New: an M card enters a fitting area, otherwise one thread; p1 and `security` set order only and never open a thread by themselves.
  - M into an area copies 「M 卡有区进区」. 合适 is how `area-lease.md` already bounds an area (lease paths, the `Pre-claim lane:` check); it adds no rule.
  - p1 and `security` as order only copies the choice and the maintainer's own 「p1，安全卡只是优先级」. It agrees with NORTH-STAR Priority 1 and 3 on `main`: security comes first, and the grade only decides queue-jumping.
  - 无则一卡一线程 is not in the maintainer's words. It is `main`'s route for an M card on a project-thread seat, kept for the one case the ruling leaves open. It alters nothing. See ③.
  - L/XL are no longer named on this line; line 121's definition (大卡 = L/XL …) still covers them. No gap.
- Line 123, S cards. 留席内 became 留席内或进区, still `mode:subagent`. This copies 「S 卡用子代理」 and answers the question's 不进区. Inside an area the work already runs through sub-agents (`area-lease.md` 区内规则), so the line now agrees with that file.
- Lines 121–122 (big cards) and 124 (disclosure discipline) are byte-identical to `main`.
  - Line 124 reads as before: its parenthesis (私密细节不得离开席位会话) pins the seat, so 也留席内 is not widened by the new 或进区 above it.
  - Line 121: see N1.
- Line 129 cut `:请审是席位交棒`. The ban itself stays on the line. The fact lives in `SKILL.md` 路径分叉 ③ (请审 = 席位交棒), which the seat reads, and in `os-dev.md` rule 2 (交棒归席位), which the thread reads; the `AGENTS.md` claim paragraph says the same. Restatement; no rule lost.
- Line 133 cut `分支约定仍是 claude/issue-N-SLUG;`. The convention lives in `AGENTS.md` Multi-agent working discipline rule 2, in `os-dev.md` rule 1 (which also says a card thread's branch is platform-designated) and in the claim template's `Branch:` line in `SKILL.md`. Restatement; no rule lost. See N2.

**`SKILL.md`**

- Line 69, the `mode:` row. Old: M and above, p1 and `security` always `thread`. New: big cards and an M card with no fitting area `thread`; p1 and `security` order only; criteria per the runbook section. It is the same copy as runbook line 120, and it now states the big-card route outright. It agrees with the runbook lines sentence by sentence and with `execution-duties.md` (S 级机械 + M ⇒ `mode:subagent`).
- Line 107 cut `裁决引文照抄不译;`. `AGENTS.md` Communication carries the rule in full (引用中文裁决时保持原文、不翻译) and outranks this file; line 106 still lists 裁决引文 as a Chinese channel. Restatement; no rule lost.

**Rule change.** Three hunks alter dispatch: runbook lines 120 and 123, and `SKILL.md` line 69. Each alteration copies the ruling's words above and adds none. The three cuts are slimming with a surviving home each. The declared `ruled` is verified.

**Sweep for other ties** (tree at the head: `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/**`, `.claude/agents/os-dev.md`, `AGENTS.md`). No other line ties p1 or `security` to `mode:thread`. Read and found to be order or lane, not thread routing:
- `coordinator.md`: p0/p1 先, and a grade change opens no thread.
- `area-lease.md`: p0/p1 先 and 插队.
- `execution-duties.md`: p1 heads a fold, p1 takes effort by its own difficulty, and the seat does not relabel a `security` card.
- `lanes/security.md`: cloud or sub-agent only.
- `area-lease.md` 留道 still lists 安全 in its closed hand-out set. That line names no thread and is outside this diff. The brief names #35792 as its carrier; that card is not among this review's inputs and was not read. Observed, not reviewed.

**Tried to break it.**
- S p1 card on a seat with no areas: line 123 keeps it in the seat as a sub-agent. No thread. Right.
- M p1 card with a fitting area: it enters the area, where `area-lease.md` lets p0/p1 jump the order. Right.
- M card that no area fits: one thread, as on `main`.
- S-size contract-changing card: big by lines 121–122, which precede line 123, so it gets a thread; `area-lease.md` bars it from an area. Right.
- Security card under disclosure discipline: line 124 keeps it in the seat. Right.

**Nits**

- N1 (nit) — `dispatch-runbook.md` line 121, 大卡同上. On `main` the line above named one route (一卡一线程), so 同上 had one meaning. That line now names two (进区, or 一卡一线程). 同上 picks the right one only through 分区亦然, the section title, `SKILL.md` line 69, and `area-lease.md` (⛔ 不入区:大卡; an area that meets a big card hands it back). The contract is unchanged and stated outright in those two files, so a routing cannot end wrong; the shorthand is weaker than it was. Spelling 一卡一线程 on line 121 costs 9 bytes against 3 of headroom, so it needs a cut of its own: a follow-up card, not this head.
- N2 (nit) — `dispatch-runbook.md` line 133. 平台例外 no longer names the rule it is an exception to; the reader finds it in `AGENTS.md`. Leave it.
